paper.title_en: Alleviating the Hubble tension with self-interacting ultralight dark matter
paper.abstract_en: We study the possibility that a self-interacting ultralight dark matter field with a characteristic energy scale $\tilde{m}\simeq 1~{\rm eV}$ can behave like an extra radiation component before recombination. This additional radiation can reduce the sound horizon of the photon-baryon fluid. A smaller sound horizon can give a higher inferred value of the present-day Hubble parameter at the background level, and thus may help reduce the Hubble tension. This effect can be obtained without adding another dark sector component besides self-interacting ULDM. A full perturbation and likelihood analysis is needed to see if the model is consistent with CMB and structure-formation data.
